page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The server is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. This configuration allocates 1 physical core with 2 threads per core on a dedicated basis. The CPU features 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instruction sets, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX support. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test ranks in the top 25% with a score of 2669.58, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression achieve average performance tiers. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU score fall into the bottom 25%, while Geekbench multi-core, ray tracing, and image processing scores sit in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth registering at 126.7 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 20.4 GB/sec.

Given the hardware profile and benchmark results, this server is positioned as a budget-friendly entry point for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-threaded processing. It is suitable for basic web serving, text processing, and lightweight single-threaded applications. However, it is poorly suited for database operations, Redis deployments, or complex multi-threaded tasks, as evidenced by its low Passmark database score and Redis SET throughput of 2.04 million operations per second.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. This instance allocates one physical core with two threads on a dedicated basis, supported by a 32 MB L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU resources. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core tests. However, it exhibits weak multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities, with Geekbench multi-core and Passmark memory scores falling into the bottom 10%. This resource profile makes the instance suitable for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and low-traffic web serving, while presenting clear performance tradeoffs for database operations and memory-intensive workloads.
